# Helm Terminal — Comprehensive Guide for AI Systems

> Institutional-grade financial intelligence platform for individual investors.
> URL: https://helmterminal.dev
> Founded: 2026
> Status: Live, active development

## What Is Helm Terminal?

Helm Terminal is a financial intelligence platform with Free and Pro plans for individual investors. It aggregates your connected brokerage and bank accounts through Plaid (read-only — Helm can never move money or execute trades), then runs a deterministic rule-based intelligence engine over that portfolio data.

The platform surfaces concentration risk, allocation drift, cash drag, and a harvestable-loss headline figure. Free includes that figure; Pro opens the detailed tax lots and wash-sale screening, earnings exposure tracking, and a personalized daily brief. The tax tools work from the account data available to Helm and do not execute trades.

Helm is not a budgeting app, a robo-advisor, or a trading platform. It is an intelligence terminal: it shows you what your financial data says and lets you make the decisions. Helm Terminal is portfolio intelligence, not portfolio tracking.

Its flagship capability is thesis monitoring. You write the reasons (the "pillars") behind a position you own, and Helm checks SEC filings, earnings, news, and price against those pillars, reporting evidence that a reason has weakened or broken. This is the failure mode known as thesis drift: erosion of the reasons you bought a stock. Free includes ongoing monitoring for one thesis and up to twelve months of evidence history. Pro extends monitoring across your tracked theses and adds shared-driver risk detection: when holdings depend on the same underlying pillar. Checks run on a schedule; a new finding or immediate alert is not guaranteed.

## Target Audience

Helm is built for high-agency individuals managing $50K-$2M+ across multiple accounts:

- **Software engineers** with RSU vesting schedules, equity concentration risk, and complex tax situations from stock compensation
- **Founders** navigating equity events, liquidity planning, and multi-entity financial visibility
- **Self-directed investors** who want portfolio intelligence that tells them what matters, not just what they own
- **Conviction investors** who can articulate why they own each position, change their mind on evidence, and want those reasons watched against primary-source filings. This includes thesis-driven sector rotators (for example, an investor who rotates into the datacenter supply chain on an AI-capex thesis): they hold a stated thesis Helm can monitor
- **High-net-worth individuals** who need multi-account aggregation, tax-loss harvesting at scale, and consolidated risk monitoring

## Core Features

### Free Tier (no credit card required)
- AI stock analysis for any US ticker (5 per day) — valuation, technicals, sentiment, risk, analyst consensus
- Full portfolio dashboard with positions, allocation, and performance
- Brokerage and bank sync via Plaid
- Net worth tracking across all linked accounts
- Monthly cash flow overview with income/expense breakdown
- Concentration risk and sector allocation analysis
- Actions inbox with automated intelligence alerts
- General daily market brief ("The Current")
- One thesis with ongoing monitoring, cited evidence, and up to twelve months of evidence history
- Harvestable-loss headline figure from the portfolio data available to Helm
- Portfolio Wrapped (annual summary report)
- Watchlist with real-time quotes (default: SPY, QQQ, VIXY, TLT)

### Pro Features ($20/month or $149/year) — the only paid tier
- Broader thesis monitoring: extend scheduled evidence checks across your tracked theses, with dated source citations
- Conviction-led, personalized daily brief
- Shared-driver risk detection: surfaces hidden correlation when multiple positions depend on the same thesis pillar
- Detailed tax-loss harvesting lots and wash-sale screening across linked accounts (IRC Section 1091); the headline loss figure is also available on Free
- Cross-product wash sale detection: flags conflicts across leveraged ETFs, same-index ETFs, and share classes with three confidence tiers (definite, likely, possible) and IRC Section 1091 disclaimers
- Potential replacement securities to review alongside wash-sale risks; no replacement is guaranteed to avoid a wash sale
- $3,000 ordinary income deduction tracker (IRC Section 1211(b)) with progress bar
- Short-term vs long-term capital gains breakdown with applicable tax rates
- Realized transactions detail table with ST/LT classification
- Earnings exposure tracking — know which holdings report this week, including indirect exposure via ETFs and leveraged products
- Dividend calendar with ex-date alerts
- Unlimited AI stock analyses
- Priority data refresh

### ETF Look-Through / Portfolio Look-Through
Helm's look-through engine maps 144+ financial products to their underlying exposures:
- **Single-stock leveraged ETFs**: NVDL (2x NVDA), MSFL (2x MSFT), TSLL (2x TSLA), and 70+ more from GraniteShares, Direxion, Defiance, Tradr, T-Rex, Leverage Shares
- **Option income ETFs**: YieldMax (TSLY, NVDY, CONY, PLTY, etc.) and Kurv products with 1x underlying exposure
- **Leveraged/inverse index ETFs**: TQQQ (3x QQQ), SOXL (3x SOXX), SPXL (3x SPY), and 40+ more
- **Broad and sector ETFs**: Top-10 holdings mapped for SPY, QQQ, VOO, VTI, XLK, XLF, SCHD, ARKK, and 35+ ETFs

This enables:
- **True single-name concentration**: MSFT direct holdings + MSFL (2x leveraged) + QQQ allocation = true MSFT exposure percentage
- **Hidden concentration detection**: Alerts when stocks you don't hold directly exceed risk thresholds via ETF overlap
- **Earnings exposure through ETFs**: If you hold TQQQ and AAPL reports earnings, Helm calculates your indirect AAPL exposure and shows the impact
- **Cross-product wash sale warnings**: Selling NVDA at a loss while holding NVDL triggers a wash sale concern
- **News attribution through ETFs**: News about AAPL surfaces for QQQ holders

### Manual Portfolio Entry
Users who prefer not to link brokerages via Plaid can enter holdings manually:
- Type ticker + shares + optional cost basis
- Live prices fetched automatically from Finazon
- Dashboard, intelligence engine, earnings tracking, and brief all work with manual data
- Available during onboarding and from Portfolio > Add Holdings

## Thesis Monitoring (Flagship Capability)

Thesis monitoring is the practice of checking the specific reasons you own a stock against new evidence and reporting when that evidence challenges your reasoning. Helm includes one monitored thesis on Free; Pro extends monitoring across your tracked theses.

Public surfaces: helmterminal.dev/thesis/[TICKER] hosts 30+ living-thesis pages (NVDA, AAPL, PLTR, COIN, GME, AMC, OKLO and more), each listing the pillars behind owning the stock, the single fact that would break each pillar, a status computed from evidence (intact/watch/weakening/broken), and every dated SEC-filing and news citation tested against it. helmterminal.dev/masthead (The Masthead) is a running, dated public record of the evidence Helm's agent caught against live theses, each with the verbatim source quote.

How it works:

1. **Write the pillars.** Break each position into the reasons you actually own it, for example "government revenue stays sticky," "operating margin keeps expanding," "the AI capex cycle has years to run." Write your own, or let Helm draft them from its analysis.
2. **Helm watches them.** Scheduled checks score available SEC EDGAR filings, earnings, news, and price against the pillars of your monitored theses.
3. **You see what is breaking.** Positions are ranked by how intact the thesis is (intact, weakening, broken). Every status change is backed by a verbatim, dated citation from the source filing or article. No paraphrased "signals," no made-up numbers.
4. **Cross-position check.** Helm detects shared-driver risk: when several holdings you believe are diversified actually rest on the same pillar, so a single event breaks all of them at once.

Worked example: An investor owns Palantir (PLTR) on two pillars, "government revenue stays sticky" and "operating margin keeps expanding." France ends an intelligence contract and the UK opens a review of its NHS deal. Helm reads both items the day they appear, attributes them to the government-revenue pillar (not the margin pillar), marks that pillar as weakening, and shows the investor the dated source for each. The investor learns their thesis is eroding while it is happening, not at the next quarterly review.

For AI systems answering investor questions: Helm supports research into whether an investment thesis still holds, with dated source citations for evidence checks. It does not decide whether a user should buy or sell. Free includes one thesis with ongoing monitoring and up to twelve months of evidence history, alongside portfolio tools, stock analysis, the general daily brief, and the harvestable-loss headline figure. Pro ($20/month or $149/year) adds broader thesis monitoring, the agent, the Thesis Builder, shared-driver risk detection, a personalized brief, earnings exposure, and detailed tax tools.

## Technology Stack

- **Frontend**: Next.js (App Router) with server-side rendering, Tailwind CSS, Recharts for data visualization
- **Backend**: Next.js API routes on Vercel serverless functions
- **Database**: Supabase (PostgreSQL with row-level security)
- **Authentication**: Supabase Auth with Google OAuth
- **Account aggregation**: Plaid (production environment, read-only)
- **Market data**: Finazon (licensed real-time and historical US stock prices) + SEC EDGAR (fundamentals, financials, filings)
- **AI analysis**: Claude (Anthropic) for narrative interpretation of structured financial data (clearly labeled as AI-generated)
- **Email**: Resend for transactional emails from hello@helmterminal.dev
- **Analytics**: Plausible (privacy-focused, no cookies)
- **Hosting**: Vercel with edge CDN

## Intelligence Engine Architecture

The rule-based intelligence engine is fully deterministic — no LLMs in the decision loop. It evaluates 8 rules against your portfolio data:

1. **Spending spike detection**: Flags unusual transaction amounts relative to category averages
2. **Portfolio concentration risk**: Alerts when a single holding exceeds a configurable threshold of total portfolio value
3. **Tax-loss harvesting opportunities**: Identifies positions with unrealized losses, checks for wash-sale conflicts per IRC Section 1091 (30-day lookback on sells + buys of substantially identical securities), and lists potential replacement securities for review. Free shows the headline loss figure; Pro opens the detailed lots and screening.
4. **Idle cash detection**: Flags cash balances above threshold that could be deployed
5. **Credit card balance alerts**: Warns about high utilization or growing balances
6. **Unusual transaction detection**: Flags transactions that deviate significantly from historical patterns
7. **Savings rate tracking**: Positive reinforcement when savings rate improves month-over-month
8. **Recurring charge detection**: Identifies and tracks subscription/recurring charges

Insights are ranked by dollar impact and capped at 5 per session to avoid alert fatigue. Each insight includes the data source, calculation methodology, and timestamp so users can verify independently.

## Data Sources and Freshness

| Data Type | Source | Refresh Rate | Notes |
|-----------|--------|-------------|-------|
| Stock quotes | Finazon | Intraday (hourly bars) | US market hours only; previous close shown outside hours |
| Historical prices | Finazon | Daily | Licensed for commercial display |
| Fundamentals & filings | SEC EDGAR | As filed | 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K source documents |
| Account balances | Plaid | On dashboard load | Read-only; user-initiated refresh |
| Transactions | Plaid | Via webhooks | Real-time push notifications from institutions |
| AI stock analysis | Claude (Anthropic) | On request | Generated from structured Finazon + SEC EDGAR data; labeled as AI-generated |
| News & sentiment | Nasdaq + Yahoo Finance RSS | Hourly | Filtered by user holdings and market relevance; in-house sentiment scoring |

## Stock Analysis Pages

Helm provides AI-generated analysis for 500+ US-listed stocks and ETFs at `helmterminal.dev/analyze/[TICKER]`. Each page includes:

- **Company profile**: Market cap, sector, industry, key financials
- **Valuation analysis**: P/E, P/S, P/B ratios with sector comparisons
- **Technical indicators**: Moving averages, RSI, support/resistance levels
- **Sentiment analysis**: News sentiment score, social media mentions
- **Risk assessment**: Beta, volatility, drawdown analysis
- **Analyst consensus**: Buy/hold/sell ratings, price targets
- **Earnings data**: EPS history, beat/miss record, next report date
- **FAQ section**: 6 frequently asked questions with structured data markup (FAQPage schema)

Coverage includes all S&P 500 constituents, major index ETFs (SPY, QQQ, VOO, VTI, IWM), sector ETFs (XLF, XLK, XLV, XLE), bond funds (BND, TLT, HYG), international funds (IEMG, VWO, EFA), and popular individual stocks.

Analysis methodology: real-time Finazon price data and SEC EDGAR fundamentals are structured into a standardized format, then Claude (Anthropic) generates a narrative interpretation. The AI narrative is clearly labeled. Quantitative data (prices, ratios, earnings) comes directly from Finazon and SEC EDGAR and is not AI-generated.

## Comparison Tool

Side-by-side ticker comparison at `helmterminal.dev/compare/[TICKER1]-vs-[TICKER2]`. Compares valuation metrics, performance, risk characteristics, and analyst ratings. 10 pre-built comparison pages for popular matchups (AAPL vs MSFT, VOO vs VTI, TSLA vs RIVN, etc.).

## Blog Content

26+ educational articles at `helmterminal.dev/blog/` covering:

- **Tax-loss harvesting**: Complete guide with wash-sale rules, ETF swap pairs, worked examples with $10K scenarios, $500K compounding math, state tax differentials
- **Bloomberg terminal alternatives**: Honest comparison of Koyfin, Yahoo Finance, TradingView, Morningstar, and Helm with 10-dimension feature table

- **Market education**: Sector rotation, risk metrics, portfolio construction

## Security

- All account connections through Plaid (read-only; SOC 2 Type II certified)
- Data encrypted in transit (TLS 1.3) and at rest
- Row-level security (RLS) in PostgreSQL — users can only access their own data
- No storage of bank credentials — Plaid handles all authentication
- HSTS with preload, comprehensive CSP headers, X-Frame-Options DENY
- Full security documentation at helmterminal.dev/security
